guide.title: Field Triage (START / JumpSTART / SALT)
guide.lead: When patients outnumber rescuers, the goal changes: do the most good for the most people. Triage fast, with simple rules, and only do life-saving interventions as you go. Then re-triage, because patients change.

steps.text: "If you can walk, come here": walkers are green (minor).
Not breathing: open the airway. Still not breathing = black.
Control major bleeding as you go.
No radial pulse or capillary refill over 2 seconds

sections.title: JumpSTART (about 1–8 years)
rows: Apneic with a pulse: 5 rescue breaths → breathing
Apneic with a pulse: 5 rescue breaths → still apneic

steps.title: Sort
steps.text: Walk; wave or move purposefully; still. Assess the still first.

steps.title: Life-saving interventions
steps.text: Control major hemorrhage, open the airway (2 rescue breaths in children), chest decompression, auto-injector antidotes.

sections.title: Running the scene
items: Roles: incident command, triage, treatment, transport, staging
First report: METHANE – major incident, exact location, type, hazards, access, number of casualties, emergency services

quiz.q: JumpSTART: apneic child with a strong pulse after airway opening. Do:
SALT: after a tourniquet and airway opening, the patient has a pulse but stays unresponsive. Category?
START: adult not breathing after the airway is opened:
quiz.explanation: No rescue breaths in adult START.

options: Major hemorrhage control, airway opening, chest decompression, auto-injector antidotes

quiz.explanation: Major incident, Exact location, Type, Hazards, Access, Number, Emergency services.

flashcards.question: RPM in START
flashcards.answer: Respirations (above 30/min = red), Perfusion (no radial pulse or refill over 2 seconds = red), Mental status (can't follow commands = red).

flashcards.question: START vs JumpSTART
flashcards.answer: JumpSTART gives 5 rescue breaths to an apneic child with a pulse: breathing = red, not black.

flashcards.question: Who gets JumpSTART?
flashcards.answer: Children about 1–8 years (a child-sized patient); adapted for infants too.

flashcards.question: SALT life-saving interventions
flashcards.answer: Control major hemorrhage, open the airway (2 rescue breaths in children), chest decompression, auto-injector antidotes.

flashcards.question: SALT
flashcards.answer: Sort, Assess, Lifesaving interventions, Treatment/Transport. Categories: immediate, delayed, minimal, expectant, dead.

flashcards.question: Triage tag
flashcards.answer: Category colour, patient ID, vital signs, treatments, decontamination status, destination.

flashcards.question: Incident roles
flashcards.answer: Incident command, triage, treatment, transport, staging.

critical.scenario: Bus rollover, about 20 patients. Eight walk to you. A man on the ground: RR 28, radial pulse, squeezes your hand on request. A woman half out of a window isn't breathing even after you open her airway.
critical.question: START categories?

options.t: Walkers green; the man yellow; the woman black
Walkers green; the man yellow; the woman red with rescue breaths
options.f: Adult START gives no rescue breaths.

options.t: Walkers yellow; the man red; the woman black
options.f: RR 28 with a pulse and commands = yellow.

critical.explanation: Hard but correct: resources go to salvageable patients.

critical.scenario: Explosion. A 7-year-old is apneic with a strong brachial pulse; after 5 rescue breaths he breathes at 28/min but doesn't respond to voice. An adult with a bleeding thigh has a weak radial pulse, RR 26, alert.
critical.question: Categories?

options.t: Child red (breathing after rescue breaths, unresponsive); adult red (bleeding with poor perfusion – tourniquet as a life-saving intervention)

options.f: The child breathes after rescue breaths.

critical.explanation: JumpSTART saves children that adult START would tag black.

critical.scenario: Highway pile-up: 3 red, 4 yellow, 6 green, 2 black; 4 ambulances on scene, a fifth in 8 minutes. One red patient becomes apneic with no pulse.
critical.question: Priority and resources?

options.t: Re-triage him as expectant/dead and send ambulances to the remaining red patients first
Send an ambulance with CPR for him now
options.f: That takes resources from salvageable patients.

options.t: Stop triage and run a resuscitation

critical.explanation: Re-triage is continuous; it's the hardest call in triage.
critical.kpi: MCI resource allocation and re-triage decisions
